transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?

I’ve noticed my eating’s been off for the past few weeks. I’ll skip breakfast and lunch without really meaning to, then just pick at dinner even if my wife cooked. My jeans are starting to feel loose, so I figured I should bring it up.
Over the past few weeks, how has your mood been?
Most days I’ve been feeling pretty heavy and flat when I wake up. The apartment feels too quiet, and even picking up my guitar doesn’t really do much for me lately.
Have you ever had a period in the past where you felt this down and flat?
Yeah. Looking back, it’s been coming and going for about three months—feeling depressed and slowed down. The last few weeks have been the most noticeable.
Have you ever experienced a period where you felt unusually energized or 'on top of the world' for days at a time?
Yeah—before this low spell, I had a stretch where I felt really fired up, like I was on a roll. I got irritated really easily, though. Little interruptions would make me snap at people.
How long have you been experiencing these alternating ups and downs in your mood?
Looking back, the depressed, slowed-down part has been coming and going for about three months. The last few weeks have felt the most noticeable.
How long did that stretch where you felt fired up and unusually energized last?
I’m not really sure how long it lasted. I didn’t keep track of it closely.
Have you noticed these ups and downs in your mood happening continuously over the past two years or more?
I’m not sure. I’ve noticed it over the past few months, but I really can’t say whether it’s been going on continuously for two years.
During that stretch when you felt fired up, did it cause any significant problems with your work, family, or daily responsibilities?
I’m still keeping up with the basic things at home, but my projects have kind of stalled. I also missed some chances to follow through with musicians I’d contacted.
During that time when you felt fired up, did you find that you needed much less sleep than usual without feeling tired?
Yeah. For several nights I only slept maybe three or four hours, but I’d wake up feeling charged anyway. It felt like sleep was just getting in the way of finishing the next track or spreadsheet.
During that energized period, did it feel like your thoughts were racing or moving much faster than usual?
I’m not really sure. I felt very focused on what I was doing, but I don’t know if my thoughts were actually moving faster than usual.
During that energized period, did you do anything unusually risky or out of character, such as spending excessive money or making impulsive decisions?
I don’t think so. I was mostly just focused on my projects—I can’t think of anything especially risky or out of character.
During this low period, have you had any thoughts of harming yourself or that you would be better off dead?
I’m not sure what you mean exactly. I’ve been feeling low, but I haven’t really noticed thoughts like that.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a current depressive episode characterized by depressed mood, anhedonia, decreased appetite with noticeable weight loss, and psychomotor slowing for the past several weeks. Prior to this episode, the patient experienced a distinct period of abnormally elevated energy, irritability, and a decreased need for sleep (sleeping 3–4 hours and feeling charged), consistent with a past hypomanic or manic episode. This pattern of alternating affective episodes fulfills the diagnostic criteria for bipolar affective disorder (F31).
